title: Arcs & sectors
examples: How do I find the length of an arc if I only know the angle in degrees?
What is the relationship between the angle in degrees and the angle in radians?
Can you show me how to calculate the area of a sector using radians?

explain.say: Today we look at parts of a circle. We will find the length of an arc. An arc is just a curved piece of the circle's edge.
The length of an arc is a fraction of the circle's total edge. The total edge is the circumference, or two times pi times the radius.
If the angle is given in degrees, you use this formula. For example, a 60 degree arc on a circle with a radius of five units.
You calculate the fraction by dividing 60 by 360. Then multiply that by two times pi times five. The arc length is approximately 5.24 units.
Next we look at radians. Radians are a unit for angles. A full circle is two pi radians.

faq.q: What is the difference between an arc and a chord?
faq.a: An arc is the curved part of the circle's edge. A chord is a straight line connecting two points on the circle.
asks: Is an arc curved or straight?
What is the straight line across a circle called?

faq.q: How do I convert an angle from degrees to radians?
faq.a: To convert degrees to radians, you multiply the degree measure by pi divided by 180. This gives you the radian measure.
asks: What is the degree to radian conversion?
How do I change degrees to radians?

faq.q: If I use radians, what is the formula for arc length?
faq.a: When using radians, the formula is much simpler. You just multiply the radius by the angle in radians. The length is r times theta.
asks: What is the easy way to find arc length?

faq.q: Does the radius change when I calculate the arc length?
faq.a: No, the radius stays the same for the entire arc. It is the fixed distance from the center to the edge.
asks: Do I use the radius anywhere?
Is the radius constant for the arc?

faq.q: What is the full circle in radians?
faq.a: A full circle always measures two pi radians. This is a key fact to remember for circle calculations.
asks: How many radians in a circle?
What is the angle measure of a full circle in radians?

facts: The circumference of a circle is always two times pi times the radius.
A full circle measures 360 degrees or two pi radians.
The formula for arc length using radians is simply r times theta.
The ratio pi is an irrational number, approximately three point one four one.

quiz.say: A sector has a radius of ten units and a central angle of ninety degrees. What is the arc length?
quiz.why: The fraction of the circle is ninety divided by three hundred sixty, which simplifies to one divided by four. Multiplying that by two times pi times ten gives pi times five.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to use the fraction of the circle's total edge.
wrong.1: This mistake calculates the full circumference instead of just the arc.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly squares the radius instead of multiplying by it.

quiz.say: Find the arc length if the radius is seven units and the angle is pi divided by three radians.

options.show: seven times pi divided by ninety
options.say: seven times pi divided by ninety

options.show: seven plus pi divided by three
options.say: seven plus pi divided by three

options.show: two times pi times seven divided by three
options.say: two times pi times seven divided by three

quiz.why: When using radians, the formula is radius times the angle. So, seven times pi divided by three is the correct length.

wrong.0: This mistake incorrectly uses the degree formula structure instead of the radian formula.
wrong.1: This mistake adds the values together instead of multiplying them.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly uses the full circumference formula instead of the radian formula.

quiz.say: What is the arc length for a radius of twelve units and a central angle of one hundred eighty degrees?
quiz.why: One hundred eighty degrees is exactly half of a circle, so the fraction is one half. Half of the circumference, two times pi times twelve, is twelve pi.

wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly squares the radius value.
wrong.2: This mistake only calculates half of the radius times pi, missing the full circumference calculation.
wrong.3: This mistake uses three times the radius instead of the correct formula.
